about.title: Marina Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Marina residents rely on all kinds of consumer, household, and workplace products every day — from cars driven along Reservation Road to tools used near Imjin Parkway job sites. When a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the person hurt often has no idea whether the responsibility lies with the manufacturer, distributor, or the retailer who sold it locally. California law gives injured people an important advantage here: strict liability. That means you generally don't have to prove the company was careless, only that the product itself was defective and that it caused your injury. If you were hurt by a defective product anywhere in Marina or elsewhere in Monterey County, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney at no cost to explore your situation, free of pressure and free of guesswork about legal jargon.

whyChoose.title: Why Marina Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Works in Your Favor
items.desc: Because California generally applies strict liability to defective products, you don't need to prove negligence — just that the defect existed and caused harm. An attorney can help identify which theory (design, manufacturing, or warning defect) fits your case.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can all be held liable under California law. An independent attorney can help sort out who was involved in getting the product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective product intact, along with packaging and receipts, can be critical to building a claim. An attorney can advise you on how to protect this evidence before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, manuals, or receipts. Don't attempt to repair it or throw it away, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims. An attorney can advise you on safe storage until it can be examined.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not usually. California's strict liability rules generally let you focus on showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving carelessness. This can make these claims more accessible than typical negligence cases.

items.question: Is this only for injuries from big companies' products?
items.answer: No — defective product claims in Marina can involve anything from household appliances to vehicle parts sold locally near Del Monte Boulevard or Imjin Pw. Local and national businesses alike can be part of the supply chain. An independent attorney can help figure out who's responsible in your specific situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys who typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You can explore your options without any upfront cost or obligation.
